(transitive) To be acquainted or familiar with; to have encountered.

know-how.gloss: The knowledge and skill to be able to (do something correctly).

knowledge.gloss: The fact of knowing about something; general understanding or familiarity with a subject, place, situation etc. [from 14th c.]

knuckle.gloss: Any of the joints between the bones of the fingers.

koala.gloss: A tree-dwelling marsupial, Phascolarctos cinereus, that resembles a small bear with a broad head, large ears and sharp claws, mainly found in eastern Australia.

kohlrabi.gloss: Brassica oleracea var. gongylodes, a variety of the cabbage, having a turnip-shaped edible stem.

koi.gloss: Ornamental domesticated varieties of the Amur carp (Cyprinus rubrofuscus), of Japan and eastern Asia with red-gold or white coloring.

kokuji.gloss: Any of the kanji characters invented in Japan.

kolkata.gloss: The capital city of West Bengal, India, formerly known in English as Calcutta.

komaki.gloss: A city in Aichi Prefecture, Japan.

komboskini.gloss: (Christianity) A rope of usually 33, 50 or 100 knots, used in meditative prayer in the Eastern Orthodox and Eastern Catholic tradition, to count one's recitations of the Jesus Prayer.

kombu.gloss: Edible (from the class Phaeophyceae) used in East Asian cuisine.

kombucha.gloss: A fermentation of sweetened tea of Mongolian origin.

komoro.gloss: A city in Nagano Prefecture, Japan.

kongo.gloss: A Bantu language (or family of languages) of Central Africa.

konstanz.gloss: A city and district in Baden-Württemberg, south Germany, on Lake Constance, and on the border with Switzerland.

kopek.gloss: A kapiejka: a Belarusian monetary unit equal to one hundredth of a ruble (rubel).

korea.gloss: A geographic region consisting of two countries in East Asia, commonly known as South Korea and North Korea; formerly a single country.

korea strait.gloss: A strait between Korea and Japan, connecting the East China Sea with the Sea of Japan.

korean.gloss: Of or relating to the Asian Peninsula comprising North Korea and South Korea.
(uncountable) Official language of the people residing on the Korean Peninsula, and language of approximately 60 million people, in Asia, North America, and elsewhere.

koreanic.gloss: Belonging to or dealing with the languages originally spoken in the Korean Peninsula.

koruna.gloss: The currency of the Czech Republic, divided into 100 hellers.

kosovo.gloss: A partly-recognized country on the Balkan Peninsula in Southeast Europe. Official name: Republic of Kosovo. Capital and largest city: Pristina. Considered by the Republic of Serbia to be one of its two autonomous provinces.

kostanay.gloss: A city on the Tobol River in northern Kazakhstan, with a population of 220,000.

koumiss.gloss: A fermented drink made from mare's milk, common among peoples of the Central Asian steppes.

kowloon.gloss: A region, peninsula, and urban area of Hong Kong.

kowtow.gloss: (figuratively) To grovel, act in a very submissive manner; to show obeisance to (someone or something) in such a manner; to bow.

kozachi laheri.gloss: A village in Oleshky urban hromada, Kherson Raion, Kherson Oblast, Ukraine, founded in 1758.

košice.gloss: The second largest city of Slovakia.

kraft paper.gloss: Strong paper made from kraft pulp, often used for making corrugated board; usually brown.

krai.gloss: (administrative division) A region or province in Russia.

kraken.gloss: (Norse mythology) A colossal sea monster that attacks ships and sailors, often portrayed as a giant octopus or squid.

krakow.gloss: A city on the Vistula River, the capital of the Lesser Poland Voivodeship in southern Poland and the former capital (until 1596) of Poland as a whole.

kraska.gloss: A village in Ratne settlement hromada, Kovel Raion, Volyn Oblast, Ukraine, founded a. 1783.

krasnaya yaruga.gloss: An urban-type settlement, the administrative centre of both the urban settlement and the raion of the same name in Belgorod Oblast, Central Federal District, Russia, first mentioned in 1681.
An urban settlement of the raion of the same name of Belgorod Oblast, Central Federal District, Russia, established in December 2004.

krasnodar.gloss: A city, the administrative center of Krasnodar Krai, Russia, called Yekaterinodar before December 1920.

krasnoyarsk.gloss: A city, the administrative center of Krasnoyarsk Krai in Siberia, Russia.

kremlin.gloss: The Moscow Kremlin; a fortified complex in Moscow, Russia that serves as the official residence of the President of the Russian Federation.

kreuzer.gloss: (historical) A small coin of varying value formerly used in parts of Germany and Austria.

krolevets.gloss: A city in Sumy Oblast, in north-eastern Ukraine.

krone.gloss: The currency of Iceland, Denmark (including Greenland and the Faroe Islands) and Norway, divided into 100 øre, except in Iceland where 1 króna = 100 aurar.

krynky.gloss: A village in Oleshky urban hromada, Kherson Raion, Kherson Oblast, Ukraine, founded in 1785.

krypton.gloss: (uncountable) The chemical element (symbol Kr) with an atomic number of 36. It is a colourless, odourless noble gas that only reacts with fluorine. It is one of the rarest gases in the Earth's atmosphere.

króna.gloss: The currency of Iceland, divided into 100 aurar

ku klux klan.gloss: An American white supremacist secret society and terrorist organization.

kuala lumpur.gloss: A federal territory, the capital and largest city of Malaysia, located in the western part of the country.

kuban.gloss: (by extension) a geographic region of Southern Russia surrounding the Kuban River, on the Black Sea between the Don Steppe, Volga delta and the Caucasus.

kudamatsu.gloss: A city in Yamaguchi Prefecture, Japan.

kugel.gloss: A traditional savoury or sweet Jewish dish consisting of a baked pudding of pasta, potatoes, or rice, with vegetables, or raisins and spices.

kumagaya.gloss: A city in Saitama prefecture, Japan.

kumquat.gloss: A small, orange citrus-like fruit which is native to Asia (Citrus japonica, syn. Fortunella japonica).

kung fu.gloss: (martial arts) The Chinese martial arts collectively.

kuomintang.gloss: A nationalist political party founded under Sun Yat-sen in 1912 that ruled mainland China from 1928 to 1949, now one of three major parties in the Republic of China (Taiwan).

kupiansk.gloss: (historical) A povit of, successively, the Voronezh Viceroyalty and then the Voronezh, Sloboda Ukraine and Kharkov Governorates of the Russian Empire, and then of the Kharkiv Governorate of the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic; establish
A city, the administrative centre of Kupiansk urban hromada, Kupiansk Raion, Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, founded in 1655.

kurayoshi.gloss: A city in Tottori Prefecture, Japan.

kurchatovium.gloss: (chemistry, physics) A rejected name for rutherfordium.

kurd.gloss: A member of the linguistically and culturally distinct people who speak Kurdish and mainly inhabit those parts of Turkey, Iran, Iraq and Syria sometimes known as Kurdistan.

kurdish.gloss: Family of Indo-Iranian languages of Kurdistan (in the Mesopotamia region, from the Zagros of mid-western Iran to the eastern extension of the chain of the Taurus Mountains).

kurdistan.gloss: A cultural region in West Asia inhabited mostly by the Kurds, encompassing parts of Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria.

kuril islands.gloss: An archipelago between Japan and Kamchatka, Russia, separating the Sea of Okhotsk from the north Pacific Ocean.

kusoge.gloss: (video games) unenjoyable or otherwise poorly-made video game. [Since 2010]

kuwait.gloss: A country in West Asia in the Middle East. Official name: State of Kuwait. Capital: Kuwait City.

kuwana.gloss: A city in Mie Prefecture, Japan.

kvass.gloss: A fermented cereal-based low alcoholic beverage, often flavored with fruit, honey and herbs.

kvetch.gloss: A person who endlessly whines or complains; a person who finds fault with anything.
To whine or complain, often needlessly and incessantly.

kyiv.gloss: The capital city of Ukraine and regional administrative centre of Kyiv Oblast.

kyrgyz.gloss: Of, from, or relating to Kyrgyzstan, the Kyrgyz people, or the Kyrgyz language
Member of a Turkic people living primarily in Kyrgyzstan
The Turkic language of the Kyrgyz people

kyrgyzstan.gloss: A country in Central Asia, bordering on Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and China. Official name: Kyrgyz Republic. Capital: Bishkek.

kyrgyzstani.gloss: Of or pertaining to Kyrgyzstan, its people and culture

kyslivka.gloss: A village in Petropavlivka rural hromada, Kupiansk Raion, Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, founded in 1710.

kythira.gloss: An island of Greece in the south-east Ionian Sea at the opening to the Aegean Sea.

kyūjitai.gloss: The traditional form of Japanese kanji used before 1947.

königsberg.gloss: (historical) The former capital of East Prussia, Germany, now Kaliningrad, Russia.

kōnan.gloss: A city in Aichi Prefecture, Japan.
A city in Kōchi Prefecture, Japan.
